summary: Builder.ai (formerly Engineer.ai), once valued at $1.5B after raising more than $450M, entered insolvency in May 2025 after its 2024 revenue proved to be a fraction of what lenders were told. US prosecutors sought its financial records, it owed large sums to cloud providers, and there are unresolved questions about how much its 'AI' was human labour. There is no operating business to invest in; any remaining interest would be a distressed-asset or litigation play.

contradictions.claim: The company told lenders it projected 2024 sales of $220M and claimed 2.3x revenue growth.
contradictions.reality: Actual 2024 revenue was about $50M (other reporting says about $55M), roughly a quarter of what was represented, which led to default and insolvency.

contradictions.claim: Natasha, an AI product manager, builds software with 'no need for an expert in the middle', making app building as easy as ordering pizza (company-written profile text).
contradictions.reality: Independent sources describe a network of human developers, mainly in India, doing custom coding, with reports of around 700 engineers. However, one independent account says Natasha did use LLMs alongside human input, so the extent of automation is disputed.

contradictions.claim: The company offers 'transparent and guaranteed pricing with no lock-in' (company-written profile text).
contradictions.reality: Reviewers report one project running 28 months against a 6-month estimate, refunds refused or replaced with credit, and customers needing third-party help to recover their code.
